_about: Records of how the town acquired, defined, or gave up its rights at each site (layouts, acceptances, deeds, gifts, purchases, takings, exchanges, releases, boundary changes), keyed by site id from sites.json. Maintenance, naming, parking and recommendation records were removed 2026-11-11. Records cite either "pages" (scan or printed page numbers; images live at {source.pagesDir}/p{page}.jpg) or a web "url". "siteMatch" records whether the link between the old record and the modern site is verified or assumed. Full citations: sources/*/FINDINGS.md

etheridge-1893.title: Copy of the Old Records of the Town of Duxbury, Mass., from 1642 to 1770
etheridge-1893.detail: Transcribed 1892 by George Etheridge; printed Plymouth: Avery & Doten, 1893. Secondary source (transcription of the original manuscript books).

tlsc-1975.title: Report of the Duxbury Town Landing Study Committee, 1975
tlsc-1975.detail: Typescript report to the Selectmen by Donald F. Corcoran, Robert Cooper and Robert S. Ramsay, appointed under Article 65 of the 1974 annual town meeting. It includes typed transcriptions of town report excerpts from 1894 to 1972. Those transcriptions are a secondary source, so check each one against the original Town Report. The page links go to pages of the scanned copy (scan page numbers, not the report's typed page numbers).

10.title: Town votes to build the highway laid out by the County Commissioners to include Mattakeesett Court; land damage paid to John A. Irwin
10.quote: Voted—That the Town proceed to build the highway laid out by the County Commissioners, and ordered built, to include Mattakeesett Court, as soon as practical
10.by: Annual town meeting March 3, 1902, Town Report p. 38 ($500 appropriated). The Mattakeesett Court account in the next report (p. 17) pays "John A. Irwin, land damage, $34 20". The County Commissioners' layout itself is not yet found Also quoted in the 1975 Town Landing Study Committee report

10.title: Town buys John A. Irwin's "upland and shore" at Mattakeesett Court for $400
10.quote: TOWN LANDING AT MATTAKEESETT COURT. Paid- John A. Irwin, upland and shore, $400 00
10.by: Committee on Town Landings 1908, Town Report p. 44 ("Mr. Irwin offers to sell the town all his salt meadow for $400.00"); the 1910 appropriation list includes "For deep water town landing on land of John A. Irwin"; payment in the 1910 accounts, Town Report p. 14. Deed book and page not given

10.title: Land exchange with Wallace C. Flagg gives the town 100 more feet of frontage; deeds passed by 1917
10.quote: agreement has been made with Mr. Wallace C. Flagg for an exchange of land on Mattakeeset Court giving the Town one hundred (100) feet more frontage on the Court.
10.by: Selectmen's Reports 1916 and 1917 p. 5; Town Meeting March 11, 1916 p. 88 ($400 appropriated). Deed book and page not given

11.title: Public bathing at Winsor Street is challenged; the Selectmen take first steps to establish a town landing there
11.quote: it is exemplified in the case of Winsor street, where the right of public bathing has been brought into question. Acting on a petition, the Board of Selectmen has already taken preliminary steps toward establishing a "Town Landing" at this point.
11.by: Report of Committee on Town Landings (Alfred E. Green, Chairman), Town Report for 1908, pp. 43–44. No layout or acceptance vote has been found yet Also quoted in the 1975 Town Landing Study Committee report

12.title: Town accepts Water Street and its extension to the shore; Charles C. Clapp gives the land
12.quote: This recommendation is made with the approval of Mr. Charles C. Clapp, who kindly gives the land for the purpose, simply asking in return that a sidewalk be constructed
12.by: Highway from Washington Street near the house of James K. Burgess "thence to the shore" accepted March 7, 1898, Town Report p. 42, "providing there is no land damage"; Report on Town Landings, Town Report for 1899, p. 36 (Clapp gives the land); extension accepted 1901. Town Clerk Plan Book 2 p. 113 Also quoted in the 1975 Town Landing Study Committee report

12.title: Town accepts the town landing laid out by the Selectmen at the end of Water Street
12.quote: Voted, to accept the town landing as laid out by the Selectmen at the end of Water street.
12.by: Special town meeting November 3, 1908, Town Report p. 55. Not in the 1975 report

13.title: Town accepts Josselyn Avenue as a highway over land of John E. Josselyn
13.quote: Voted To accept Highway as laid out by the Selectmen February 11, 1907, commencing at South Station Street and running Easterly over land of John E. Josselyn
13.by: Annual town meeting March 4, 1907, Town Report p. 52 (layout by the Selectmen Feb 11, 1907, "to easterly corner of land of Mrs. Hawkins"). The 1975 report lists "Josselyn Avenue" as a town landing

14.title: Town accepts a change in the layout of the way from Washington Street through land of the Sisters of St. Margaret
14.quote: Voted, To accept the change made in the layout of the way From Washington Street through land now owned by the Sisters Saint Margaret and formerly Baldwin
14.by: Town Report for the year ending Jan 1, 1904, p. 58. That this is the way to the Harden Hill landing is assumed: the 1941 vote naming "Hardin Hill Road" (Art. 32, Town Report p. 136) describes it as the street "on the Southerly side of Washington Street beginning at the West Boundary of land of St. Margaret's and following to the Town Landing". Plan: Town of Duxbury Plan Book 1 p. 17

15.title: Town accepts "the road and landing near Allen's Wharf" as laid out by the Selectmen
15.quote: Voted to accept the road and landing near Allen's Wharf, so-called, as laid out by the Selectmen.
15.by: Annual town meeting March 4, 1895, Art. 10, Town Report p. 49. The 1975 report dates this 1896 (the report year) and identifies it as Howland's Lane. Plan: Town of Duxbury Plan Book 1 p. 16. NOTE: NSRWA says the town bought the land in 1894; not reconciled

15.title: Vote to take or buy three parcels beside "Town Landing Road" at Howland's fails (two-thirds needed); the article gives the landing's side lines by bearing
15.quote: thence turning and running N. 30° 40' E. by said Northwesterly line of Town Landing Road, protracted Southwesterly into Kingston Bay and by the Northwesterly line of Town Landing Road, 381.60 feet to the cement bound at the point of beginning.
15.by: Annual town meeting 1954, Art. 22, Town Report pp. 102–104: "Voted Down. (Yes 262, No 162 — two-thirds vote necessary)". Parcels from Land Court Plans 10966A (1925) and 15679A (1934). The same article came back about 1965 and its outcome is not yet checked. No land changed hands under this vote

16.title: Committee recommends a landing through the Foote and Crosby property on the east side of Border Street
16.quote: recommend that a public town landing be established through property owned by the Foote's and the Crosby's
16.by: Report on Town Landings, Town Report 1906 p. 39 (A. E. Green, C. F. Allen, J. H. Glover). The 1975 committee files this under Landing Road

16.title: Town votes to lay out a landing "through the property of Mrs. Foote" and appropriates $500
16.quote: Voted That the Selectmen lay out a Town Landing at "Hicks Point" so-called, and another through the property of Mrs. Foote.
16.by: Annual town meeting March 8, 1909, Town Report p. 64 ($500 appropriated) Also quoted in the 1975 Town Landing Study Committee report

16.title: Town accepts the town landing and the way to it, laid out by the Selectmen over land of E. A. D. Foote
16.quote: Voted, unanimously, to accept the Town Landing and way leading to same as laid out by the Selectmen over land of E. A. D. Foote.
16.by: Special town meeting September 2, 1909, Town Report p. 65. Town of Duxbury Plan Book 2 p. 148 is dated 9/12/09. Not in the 1975 report

16.title: Selectmen authorized to relocate Landing Road to the satisfaction of Timothy Coughlin
16.quote: Voted, to give the Selectmen authority to relocate the Landing Road to the satisfaction of Mr. Timothy Coughlin and the Selectmen.
16.by: Annual town meeting March 1, 1924. Whether the relocation was made, and its plan, are not yet found

16.title: Town takes Foote Shore Lots U and T (Block P) by eminent domain to enlarge the beach at the south end of Landing Road
16.quote: Under Article 42, it was voted that the Selectmen be authorized to take all necessary steps to take by Eminent Domain, Foote Shore Lots U and T shown on Block P of the Duxbury Assessors' Map, for the purpose of enlarging the beach area at the Southerly end of Landing Road. (Vote: 233 Yes; 0 No).
16.by: Annual town meeting March 9, 1957, Art. 42, Town Report pp. 118–119. Background (Selectmen's report, 1956, p. 15): a gift of land at the foot of Landing Road had been accepted, but an abutter later acquired title through an heir of a previous owner. The order of taking is not yet found at the Registry

17.title: Committee recommends a landing through land of Harrison Loring, "known as Hick's Point"
17.quote: another through land owned by Mr. Harrison Loring, known as Hick's Point, both being on the easterly side of Border street
17.by: Report on Town Landings, Town Report 1906 p. 39 (A. E. Green, C. F. Allen, J. H. Glover)

17.title: Town votes that the Selectmen lay out a landing at Hicks Point and appropriates $500
17.quote: Voted That the Selectmen lay out a Town Landing at "Hicks Point" so-called, and another through the property of Mrs. Foote.
17.by: Annual town meeting March 8, 1909, Town Report p. 64 ($500 appropriated). The 1908 Committee report notes the Legislature, at Duxbury's initiative, authorized towns to lay out highways to low water mark Also quoted in the 1975 Town Landing Study Committee report

17.title: Town accepts the town landing and the way to it, laid out by the Selectmen over land of Joshua B. Weston, David H. Chandler and The Loring Company
17.quote: Voted, unanimously, to accept the Town Landing and way leading to same as laid out by the Selectmen, over land of Joshua B. Weston, David H. Chandler and The Loring Company.
17.by: Special town meeting September 2, 1909, Town Report p. 65. Same meeting accepted the Foote landing (16 Landing Road), so this one is taken to be Hicks Point; assumed from the March 1909 vote. Not in the 1975 report

01.title: Town accepts the highway from Cut Island to the Hummock at Duxbury Beach and appropriates $500 to build it
01.quote: Voted To accept the Highway from the South End of Cut Island to the North end of Hummock as laid out by the Selectmen
01.by: Town Reports 1897 p. 45 (Art. 9) and 1898 p. 52, under the petition of B. S. Bryant and others. The 1975 committee files this under Ford's Stand; no layout of the landing itself is cited

02.title: Deed: Town of Duxbury to George Loring (Plymouth Deeds Book 215, p. 28); part of the landing conveyed, the rest reserved to the town forever
02.quote: it is expressly stated by deed, Dec. 30, 1843 — Plymouth Deeds, book 215, page 28 — Town of Duxbury to George Loring, that the present landing place shall be forever reserved to the town.
02.by: Plymouth Deeds Book 215, Page 28, Town of Duxbury to George Loring, after the town meeting of Nov 13, 1843. Cited in the 1899 Report on Town Landings, Town Report p. 39. Deed not yet seen

02.title: Town accepts the highway from the end of Cove Street to the top of Abram's Hill (the "new town road" that the 1899 report says borders the Old Cove landing)
02.quote: Voted, To accept the highway as laid out by the Selectmen, commencing at the end of Cove street, thence to top of "Abram's Hill," so called.
02.by: Annual town meeting March 7, 1898, Town Report p. 42

02.title: 1899 Report on Town Landings lists this as landing No. 5; the town adopts the landings as surveyed by Laurence Bradford and orders the surveys recorded at Plymouth
02.quote: At Old Cove, bordering on land now belonging to Samuel Weston and others, by new town road leading to Abrams Hill and on right of way extending around the foot of said hill by Duck Hill river.
02.by: Report on Town Landings by Laurence Bradford and Hamilton Wadsworth, Jan 21, 1899, Town Report pp. 38–41; adopted at the annual town meeting March 6, 1899 (p. 41: "that the town adopt the town landings as laid out by Mr. Bradford, that they be marked by proper stones, and the surveys be recorded in Plymouth and Town Clerk's office"). The recorded survey is Registry Plan Book 2 p. 6, per the 1975 report. The report also says this landing is dated 1834 on the town books and is "the most valuable one that the town possesses"

02.title: Town votes to exchange land at the Old Cove landing with Helen Ripley Clapp and Clara Ripley Evans
02.quote: Voted, to exchange a piece of land at Town Landing at Old Cove, so-called, for a piece adjoining said Town Landing, now belonging to Mrs. Helen Ripley Clapp and Mrs. Clara Ripley Evans.
02.by: Annual town meeting March 1, 1924, Town Report p. 72 (tabled March 17, 1923 as Art. 35). Exchange deed not yet found Also quoted in the 1975 Town Landing Study Committee report

03.title: 1899 Report on Town Landings lists this as landing No. 4; the town adopts the landings as surveyed by Laurence Bradford and orders the surveys recorded at Plymouth
03.quote: At foot of lane through land now belonging to E. F. Adams, near what was formerly Drew's salt works, at Duck Hill river.
03.by: Report on Town Landings by Laurence Bradford and Hamilton Wadsworth, Jan 21, 1899, Town Report pp. 38–41; adopted at the annual town meeting March 6, 1899 (p. 41: "that the town adopt the town landings as laid out by Mr. Bradford, that they be marked by proper stones, and the surveys be recorded in Plymouth and Town Clerk's office"). The recorded survey is Registry Plan Book 2 p. 6, per the 1975 report. Dated 1834 on the town books

03.title: Mrs. Ellen F. Adams allowed to move the way to the landing to the east side of her property
03.quote: Voted, To grant Mrs. Ellen F. Adams the right to change the way through her property to the landing, to run on the easterly side of her property, to be built to the satisfaction and acceptance of the Selectmen.
03.by: Annual town meeting March 6, 1905, Town Report p. 68. The 1975 report dates this 1904 (the warrant year). That "the landing" is No. 4 is assumed from the 1899 report, which places No. 4 through land of E. F. Adams

04.title: 1899 Report on Town Landings lists this as landing No. 3; the town adopts the landings as surveyed by Laurence Bradford and orders the surveys recorded at Plymouth
04.quote: At foot of lane through land formerly belonging to Simeon Soule, by Duck Hill river.
04.by: Report on Town Landings by Laurence Bradford and Hamilton Wadsworth, Jan 21, 1899, Town Report pp. 38–41; adopted at the annual town meeting March 6, 1899 (p. 41: "that the town adopt the town landings as laid out by Mr. Bradford, that they be marked by proper stones, and the surveys be recorded in Plymouth and Town Clerk's office"). The recorded survey is Registry Plan Book 2 p. 6, per the 1975 report. Dated 1803 and 1834 on the town books ("a very old town landing")

05.title: 1899 Report on Town Landings lists this as landing No. 2; the town adopts the landings as surveyed by Laurence Bradford and orders the surveys recorded at Plymouth
05.quote: At foot of lane by land formerly belonging to Reuben and Clark Peterson, by Duck Hill river.
05.by: Report on Town Landings by Laurence Bradford and Hamilton Wadsworth, Jan 21, 1899, Town Report pp. 38–41; adopted at the annual town meeting March 6, 1899 (p. 41: "that the town adopt the town landings as laid out by Mr. Bradford, that they be marked by proper stones, and the surveys be recorded in Plymouth and Town Clerk's office"). The recorded survey is Registry Plan Book 2 p. 6, per the 1975 report. Dated 1834 on the town books

06.title: Selectmen to lay out the way into Powder Point; gate allowed only if a good cart way is kept open
06.quote: provided the said Alden gives or allows a good cart way through his way as is usual, into Powder Point

06.title: 1899 Report on Town Landings lists this as landing No. 1; the town adopts the landings as surveyed by Laurence Bradford and orders the surveys recorded at Plymouth
06.quote: No. I is of recent origin, having been laid out by the County Commissioners in January, 1870. One of the marks being a stone bound that is still standing, the lines were easily defined.
06.by: Report on Town Landings by Laurence Bradford and Hamilton Wadsworth, Jan 21, 1899, Town Report pp. 38–41; adopted at the annual town meeting March 6, 1899 (p. 41: "that the town adopt the town landings as laid out by Mr. Bradford, that they be marked by proper stones, and the surveys be recorded in Plymouth and Town Clerk's office"). The recorded survey is Registry Plan Book 2 p. 6, per the 1975 report. The same meeting voted "That the town landing at Point End be recorded as a 'Highway to the sea,' to conform to the lay out of the County Commissioners"

06.title: Quitclaim exchange with F. B. Knapp at Point End along the County Commissioners' line: voted 1900, reversed 1902
06.quote: Voted—That the Selectmen be instructed not to give F. B. Knapp a quit claim deed for any land that is left between the road to be built at Point End and the County Commissioners line over the Cliff for a similar deed from him of the land to be used as a road.
06.by: Annual town meeting March 5, 1900 (vote to exchange quitclaim deeds); reconsidered and reversed at the annual town meeting March 3, 1902, Town Report p. 38. Same meeting accepted "Upland Road" and "Bayside Road" at Point End Also quoted in the 1975 Town Landing Study Committee report

07.title: Selectmen to lay out the way into Powder Point; gate allowed only if a good cart way is kept open
07.quote: provided the said Alden gives or allows a good cart way through his way as is usual, into Powder Point

07.title: 1899 Report on Town Landings lists this as landing No. 1; the town adopts the landings as surveyed by Laurence Bradford and orders the surveys recorded at Plymouth
07.quote: No. I is of recent origin, having been laid out by the County Commissioners in January, 1870. One of the marks being a stone bound that is still standing, the lines were easily defined.
07.by: Report on Town Landings by Laurence Bradford and Hamilton Wadsworth, Jan 21, 1899, Town Report pp. 38–41; adopted at the annual town meeting March 6, 1899 (p. 41: "that the town adopt the town landings as laid out by Mr. Bradford, that they be marked by proper stones, and the surveys be recorded in Plymouth and Town Clerk's office"). The recorded survey is Registry Plan Book 2 p. 6, per the 1975 report. The same meeting voted "That the town landing at Point End be recorded as a 'Highway to the sea,' to conform to the lay out of the County Commissioners"

07.title: Quitclaim exchange with F. B. Knapp at Point End along the County Commissioners' line: voted 1900, reversed 1902
07.quote: Voted—That the Selectmen be instructed not to give F. B. Knapp a quit claim deed for any land that is left between the road to be built at Point End and the County Commissioners line over the Cliff for a similar deed from him of the land to be used as a road.
07.by: Annual town meeting March 5, 1900 (vote to exchange quitclaim deeds); reconsidered and reversed at the annual town meeting March 3, 1902, Town Report p. 38. Same meeting accepted "Upland Road" and "Bayside Road" at Point End Also quoted in the 1975 Town Landing Study Committee report

09.title: Old landing place laid out as a common town landing; 40 ft highway to the Marshfield–Plymouth road
09.quote: allowing all the ground on the Southerly side of the said fence to bluefish river channel, for a common landing place for said town
09.by: Selectmen Edward Southworth, John Simons Sen., John Partridge; recorded by John Wadsworth, Town Clerk

09.title: Town meeting: Abraham Samson may gate the highway, and grants the town the landing privilege forever
09.quote: the benefit and privilege of the said landing place for the landing and carrying away their hay &c forever

09.title: 1899 Report on Town Landings lists this as landing No. 6; the town adopts the landings as surveyed by Laurence Bradford and orders the surveys recorded at Plymouth
09.quote: At Mill pond, by Blue Fish river, by town highway adjoining land formerly belonging to Amherst A. Frazer.
09.by: Report on Town Landings by Laurence Bradford and Hamilton Wadsworth, Jan 21, 1899, Town Report pp. 38–41; adopted at the annual town meeting March 6, 1899 (p. 41: "that the town adopt the town landings as laid out by Mr. Bradford, that they be marked by proper stones, and the surveys be recorded in Plymouth and Town Clerk's office"). The recorded survey is Registry Plan Book 2 p. 6, per the 1975 report. The report calls it "the oldest landing in the town being first defined in 1715", re-defined 1822 and 1834, and says part was sold to Samuel A. Frazer and others on Dec 30, 1840, Plymouth Deeds Book 201, Page 87 (deed not yet seen). The 1975 report ties No. 6 to St. George Street, not this site

09.title: The town owns part of the wharf at Blue River Bridge; J. H. Killian offers to transfer the rest, to revert if the town ever gives up the wharf
09.quote: the present owner of the other part, Mr. J. H. Killian, generously offers to transfer his part to the town provisionally upon the wharf being put and maintained in good repair, and further providing, that should the town ever surrender its rights to the wharf, that the property revert to him or his heirs.
09.by: Report on Town Landings (A. E. Green, Laurence Bradford, Hamilton Wadsworth), Town Report for 1899, pp. 35–36; warrant Art. 11, 1900. Whether the town accepted is not yet found

09.title: Committee on Town Landings authorized to settle the question of the St. George Street landing and to buy adjoining land
09.quote: Voted — That the committee on Town Landings be authorized to settle the question of the Town Landing on St. George street, employing counsel, if necessary, and to buy adjoining land.
09.by: Annual town meeting March 4, 1901. The 1975 report ties St. George Street to 1899 landing No. 6 at the Mill Pond; whether it is this site is open Also quoted in the 1975 Town Landing Study Committee report

09.title: Selectmen authorized to move the south line of the town land at Blue Fish River two feet north
09.quote: Voted to authorize the Selectmen to rectify the southerly line of the town land between Blue Fish River and Riverview Avenue, moving the boundary stones two feet northerly.
09.by: Town Meeting March 11, 1916, Town Report 1916 p. 90

WW-01.title: Town Meeting accepts Eben H. Ellison's deed of the upland and beach, to low water mark, restricted to Duxbury residents and their guests
WW-01.quote: Said premises are conveyed subject to the restriction that they shall be used only for recreational purposes and be restricted to the use of the residents of Duxbury and their guests; and to the further restriction that no pier shall be erected on said premises.
WW-01.by: Annual town meeting March 4, 1944, Art. 24, Town Report pp. 108–109. The deed conveys "all right, title and interest" in Somerville Avenue and the 16-foot lane on the I. L. Rich plan, Registry Plan Book 1 p. 9. Deed book and page not yet found Also quoted in the 1975 Town Landing Study Committee report

WW-02.title: Town accepts the Standish Shore ways (Elder Brewster, Samoset, Sagamore and Massasoit Roads) as laid out by the Selectmen
WW-02.quote: Voted, to accept the ways at Standish Shore, as laid out by the Selectmen February 11, 1907. Columbus Avenue, leading from southwest corner of land of Caroline C. Rushton. Brewster Road, Samoset Road, Sagamore Road and Massasoit Road, all leading from Columbus Avenue to the shore.
WW-02.by: Annual town meeting March 4, 1907, Town Report p. 53. $500 was voted April 17, 1907 for "the roads on the Porter Shore property accepted by the town at the last annual town meeting" Also quoted in the 1975 Town Landing Study Committee report

WW-02.title: Proposed re-layout of the Porter Shore roads; the original plans are Registry Plan Book 1 p. 227 (1901) and Plan Book 2 p. 290 (1903)
WW-02.quote: This plan shows Puritan Road and the four parallel roads from it to the shore, Elder Brewster, Samoset, Sagamore and Massasoit.
WW-02.by: Town Report for 1920, "Proposed Re-Layout of Porter Shore Roads"

WW-03.title: Town accepts the Standish Shore ways (Elder Brewster, Samoset, Sagamore and Massasoit Roads) as laid out by the Selectmen
WW-03.quote: Voted, to accept the ways at Standish Shore, as laid out by the Selectmen February 11, 1907. Columbus Avenue, leading from southwest corner of land of Caroline C. Rushton. Brewster Road, Samoset Road, Sagamore Road and Massasoit Road, all leading from Columbus Avenue to the shore.
WW-03.by: Annual town meeting March 4, 1907, Town Report p. 53. $500 was voted April 17, 1907 for "the roads on the Porter Shore property accepted by the town at the last annual town meeting" Also quoted in the 1975 Town Landing Study Committee report

WW-03.title: Proposed re-layout of the Porter Shore roads; the original plans are Registry Plan Book 1 p. 227 (1901) and Plan Book 2 p. 290 (1903)
WW-03.quote: This plan shows Puritan Road and the four parallel roads from it to the shore, Elder Brewster, Samoset, Sagamore and Massasoit.
WW-03.by: Town Report for 1920, "Proposed Re-Layout of Porter Shore Roads"

WW-03.title: Town instructs the Selectmen to lay out part of Samoset Road as a public highway
WW-03.quote: Voted that the Town instruct the Selectmen to lay out as a public highway that part of Samoset Road
WW-03.by: Annual town meeting March 1, 1941, Art. 36, Town Report p. 136. Plan: "A part of the Old Standish and Elder Brewster Farms", Registry Plan Book 2 p. 290. Registry Plan Book 11 p. 561 (Samoset Rd Taking, Feb 5 1942) is probably the resulting layout Also quoted in the 1975 Town Landing Study Committee report

WW-04.title: Town accepts the Standish Shore ways (Elder Brewster, Samoset, Sagamore and Massasoit Roads) as laid out by the Selectmen
WW-04.quote: Voted, to accept the ways at Standish Shore, as laid out by the Selectmen February 11, 1907. Columbus Avenue, leading from southwest corner of land of Caroline C. Rushton. Brewster Road, Samoset Road, Sagamore Road and Massasoit Road, all leading from Columbus Avenue to the shore.
WW-04.by: Annual town meeting March 4, 1907, Town Report p. 53. $500 was voted April 17, 1907 for "the roads on the Porter Shore property accepted by the town at the last annual town meeting" Also quoted in the 1975 Town Landing Study Committee report

WW-04.title: Proposed re-layout of the Porter Shore roads; the original plans are Registry Plan Book 1 p. 227 (1901) and Plan Book 2 p. 290 (1903)
WW-04.quote: This plan shows Puritan Road and the four parallel roads from it to the shore, Elder Brewster, Samoset, Sagamore and Massasoit.
WW-04.by: Town Report for 1920, "Proposed Re-Layout of Porter Shore Roads"

WW-05.title: Town accepts the Standish Shore ways (Elder Brewster, Samoset, Sagamore and Massasoit Roads) as laid out by the Selectmen
WW-05.quote: Voted, to accept the ways at Standish Shore, as laid out by the Selectmen February 11, 1907. Columbus Avenue, leading from southwest corner of land of Caroline C. Rushton. Brewster Road, Samoset Road, Sagamore Road and Massasoit Road, all leading from Columbus Avenue to the shore.
WW-05.by: Annual town meeting March 4, 1907, Town Report p. 53. $500 was voted April 17, 1907 for "the roads on the Porter Shore property accepted by the town at the last annual town meeting" Also quoted in the 1975 Town Landing Study Committee report

WW-05.title: Proposed re-layout of the Porter Shore roads; the original plans are Registry Plan Book 1 p. 227 (1901) and Plan Book 2 p. 290 (1903)
WW-05.quote: This plan shows Puritan Road and the four parallel roads from it to the shore, Elder Brewster, Samoset, Sagamore and Massasoit.
WW-05.by: Town Report for 1920, "Proposed Re-Layout of Porter Shore Roads"

WW-05.title: Selectmen instructed to lay out Massasoit Road and Mayflower Avenue as a public highway to near the Myles Standish cellar
WW-05.quote: Voted To instruct Selectmen to lay out as a public highway, Massasoit Road and Mayflower Avenue from Columbus Avenue to a point near the old Myles Standish cellar.
WW-05.by: Annual town meeting March 13, 1920, Town Report p. 83. Registry Plan Book 11 p. 555 (Massasoit Rd Taking, Feb 25 1921) is probably the resulting layout Also quoted in the 1975 Town Landing Study Committee report

WW-06.title: Captain's Nook highway (30 ft) and a cart way down to the Bay through the Standish farm
WW-06.quote: a convenient cart way is allowed down to the Bay through the farm of said Standish, which is also allowed by said Standish's consent
WW-06.by: Selectmen Edward Southworth, John Simons, John Partridge

WW-06.title: Captain's Nook highway re-laid with compass bearings; way through Capt. Wait Wadsworth's land down to the salt bay
WW-06.quote: there is a way through Capt. Wait Wadsworth's land, down to the salt bay, where it may be the most beneficial and least prejudicial to each other, forever
WW-06.by: Selectmen Ezra Arnold, John Wadsworth; accepted at Town Meeting

WW-06.title: Town accepts the homesite of Myles Standish from the Standish Monument Association
WW-06.quote: Voted unanimously that the Town accept the homesite of Myles Standish, at Standish Shore, and send thanks to the Trustees of the Standish Monument Association.
WW-06.by: Annual town meeting March 1, 1930, Art. 15. Plan: Town of Duxbury Plan Book 2 p. 144 ("Old Myles Standish Homestead including Shore Way to water"). Deed from the Standish Monument Association not yet found Also quoted in the 1975 Town Landing Study Committee report

WW-07.title: Town accepts Longview Road as laid out by the Selectmen, from Captain's Hill Road to Midway Road
WW-07.quote: Under Article 32, Voted, to accept Longview Road as laid out by the Selectmen, from Captain's Hill Road to Midway Road, so-called, and raise and appropriate $800.00 to construct the same. (Yes 76, No 67).
WW-07.by: Annual town meeting March 14, 1953, Art. 32, Town Report p. 90. Registry Plan Book 11 p. 455 (Captains' Hill & Long View Rds Taking, Jul 10 1952) is probably the layout plan

WW-07.title: Town accepts the rest of Longview Road, from Midway Road to the shore
WW-07.quote: Under Article 52, it was voted to accept the remaining portion of Longview Road from Midway Road to the Shore, and raise and appropriate the sum of $350.00 for construction of the same.
WW-07.by: Annual town meeting March 10, 1956, Art. 52, Town Report p. 151. Registry Plan Book 11 pp. 470 and 554 (Longview Rd Taking, Feb 20 1956) are probably the layout plans

WW-08.title: Town accepts Midway Road and Elderberry Lane as laid out by the Selectmen
WW-08.quote: Under Article 5, it was voted unanimously to accept Midway Road and Elderberry Lane as laid out by the Selectmen and appropriate from available funds in the Treasury the sum of $3,000.00 to construct the same.
WW-08.by: Special town meeting August 12, 1955, Art. 5, Town Report p. 116. Whether the layout runs to the water is not yet checked against a plan

WW-09.title: Town votes to acquire Bay Farm (about 44 acres, Block P) for recreation; $200,000
WW-09.quote: acquire in Fee simple by purchase, or eminent domain, if necessary, for recreational purposes
WW-09.by: Annual town meeting March 11, 1972, Art. 21, Town Report pp. 36–37 (vote 413–97). Lot 25 is Land Court Plan 14792-6, filed with Certificate No. 47518 Also quoted in the 1975 Town Landing Study Committee report
